title: Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin-glass optimization

problem.name: Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin-glass optimization
problem.statement_latex:
For independent standard Gaussian couplings $J_{ij}$, minimize $H(z)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}z_i z_j$ over $z\in\{-1,1\}^n$. One may request the exact ground state or an energy within $\varepsilon n$ of it. Random fully connected spin glasses are an average-case optimization benchmark.
Quantum circuits are measured in gates and samples; the Gaussian classical approximation theorem counts real-arithmetic operations, while exact discretized instances use bit complexity.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(pn^2)$ gates per sample, depth-$p$ QAOA for the SK Hamiltonian.
quantum.headline_text: $O(pn^2)$ gates per sample, depth-$p$ QAOA for the SK Hamiltonian.
quantum.details_latex: The infinite-size expected-energy analysis can be evaluated classically in $O(16^p)$ time for fixed parameters. It predicts the achieved energy density and guides angle selection. Exact optimization by generalized short-path algorithms uses additional overlap, spectral and landscape hypotheses, with runtime relative to an associated classical Markov-chain search.

classical.headline_latex: $C(\varepsilon)n^2$ arithmetic operations for an $\varepsilon n$-near optimum, Montanari\textquotesingle s incremental approximate message passing.
classical.headline_text: $C(\varepsilon)n^2$ arithmetic operations for an $\varepsilon n$-near optimum, Montanari's incremental approximate message passing.
classical.details_latex: The guarantee assumes full replica symmetry breaking and holds with high probability over Gaussian couplings. For exact optimization, enumeration supplies $O(n^2 2^n)$ arithmetic time, with instance-specific branch-and-bound improvements. Discretizing dense couplings to $b$ bits gives an energy-threshold circuit of size $O(n^2b)$; sparse exact counting on that circuit costs $\operatorname{poly}(n,b)2^{O(n^2b/\sqrt{\log(n^2b)})}$. The smaller exact bound is chosen for the represented instance.

strength.description_latex: The QAOA energy-density results have a polynomial-time classical near-optimal comparator. A general asymptotic QAOA advantage is unestablished.

evidence.description_latex: The limiting QAOA formulas and conditional classical approximation theorem are analytical results; empirical comparisons concern fixed depths and finite instances.

hardware.description_latex: QAOA uses $n$ data qubits but $\Theta(n^2)$ interactions per layer before compilation. Small processor experiments exist; dense routing, two-qubit errors and repeated shots determine practical cost.
